newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal received wartime gold from Swiss - report.
newsitem.headline: Portugal received wartime gold from Swiss - report.

text.p: Portugal told U.S. authorities that it had received 117.4 tonnes of gold during World War Two from the Swiss National Bank, under fire for buying Nazi German bullion, a Lisbon newspaper reported on Monday.

Diario de Noticias quoted U.S. State Department documents recently made public as saying that the Portuguese Foreign Ministry told the U.S. embassy in Lisbon in 1946 that it had received the gold between January 1939 and February 1944.
The paper said it had learned that the United States believed that the gold had been laundered by Switzerland after being confiscated by the Nazis from the Belgian, Dutch and Czech governments.

It quoted a document from the U.S. secret services dated December 6 1946 as saying: "The Portuguese admit having received gold from Germany (via Switzerland) worth $45 million and $67 million in cash from Switzerland (possibly originating from Germany)."
Diario de Noticias said the gold would be worth almost 200 billion escudos ($1.27 billion) at current prices.
Portuguese central bank spokesman Vitor Martins said of the newspaper report: "The Bank of Portugal has no comment."
In October the Bank of Portugal did not comment on reports that Portugal tried to use looted Nazi gold to buy coal from Poland in the winter of 1946.
Portugal, not Switzerland, may have been the recipient of the largest unaccounted-for chunk of gold stolen by the Nazis in World War Two, the U.S. magazine Newsweek reported in October.
